name: MAX6350ESA+T
title: 1 ppm/°C low-noise 2.5 V, 4.096 V and 5 V voltage references
summary: MAX6325, MAX6341 and MAX6350 are series voltage references built on a buried zener, giving 2.5 V, 4.096 V and 5 V from an 8 V to 36 V supply. Drift is 0.5 ppm/°C typical and 1 ppm/°C at most in the C grade, initial error ±0.02% for the MAX6350, and the output sources or sinks up to 15 mA. NR and TRIM pins allow optional noise filtering and output adjustment. Intended uses include 16-bit data converters, reference standards, process control, digital voltmeters, ATE and precision current sources.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The reference alone: an 8 V to 36 V supply on IN, the reference taken from OUT, NR and TRIM unconnected. A 2.2 µF capacitor on the input and another on the output are both optional.

circuits.title: +5 V and -5 V references from one +5 V supply (Figure 3)
circuits.description: A MAX865 charge pump turns a single +5 V input into rails of roughly +9 V and -9 V. The MAX6350 runs from the positive rail and gives +5 V; a MAX400 op amp, its + input grounded, inverts that through R2 and R4 to give -5 V. R2 and R4 are matched in value and in temperature coefficient. R1 trims both outputs together; R3 sets the negative one. C4 sits from the op amp output back to its inverting input.

where.ΔVOUT(max): largest spread of output voltage over the temperature range

operation.text: Three fixed-output buried-zener references share one die design and pinout: MAX6325 at 2.5 V, MAX6341 at 4.096 V, MAX6350 at 5 V. Each has optional noise-reduction and output-trim pins. Grades C, E and M differ in temperature range and in the guaranteed tempco (1.0, 1.5 and 2.5 ppm/°C max).
A temperature-compensation scheme drawing little power keeps the output curve nearly flat over temperature without heating the die.
With a 10 kΩ potentiometer from OUT to GND and its wiper on TRIM, the output moves by at least 0.6%. Trimming leaves the temperature stability unchanged. TRIM is left open when unused.
A 1 µF capacitor on NR lowers wideband noise; going above 1 µF brings little further gain. Noise on the supply also reaches the output, and an optional capacitor from IN to GND reduces it.
The output is stable with any load capacitance from 0 µF to 100 µF at any load current. A capacitor on OUT helps against noise and against glitches when the load steps.
Load regulation is guaranteed for currents up to 15 mA, both sourced and sunk.
OUT may be shorted to GND indefinitely with VIN at or below 12 V, but for no more than 5 s with VIN up to 40 V. A short from OUT to IN is allowed indefinitely with VIN at or below 12 V.
In Figure 3 a low-offset op amp inverts the +5 V output to make a matching -5 V. A charge pump makes about ±9 V from a single unregulated +5 V supply to run both the reference and the op amp.
